findings.claim: On the starter run, the Task 5 failure prints the full expected grid area map as an assertion diff (header/header, main/aside, footer/footer). It is outcome-shaped data rather than a declaration, but it maps one-to-one onto the grid-template-areas value the learner is meant to compose, so the retry feedback hands over more of the Task 5 rule than the README hints do. Evidence: Scratch copy of HEAD 9ad7bb04c287912d37605ba365b448f0fd68cd88 under $TMPDIR, npm ci then node --test --test-reporter=spec: 0/11 pass; Task 5 message 'From 1000px wide, the named regions do not yet form the required page layout.' followed by 'expected: [ [ 'header', 'header' ], [ 'main', 'aside' ], [ 'footer', 'footer' ] ]'. tests/layout.test.mjs lines 79-80 use assert.deepEqual with that literal as expected. All other starter failure messages are outcome-first and name no completed declaration beyond what the README task already states.
findings.recommendation: Optional: compare the area map with a boolean or a custom message (for example report which region is misplaced at 1100px) so the diff does not print the full expected map; keep the outcome-first sentence.

findings.claim: The headline sizes the ten required tasks against the 40-minute block, but does not say whether reading the README, the one-time npm ci with its about 200 MB Chromium download, and the first full test run sit inside or before the block. With all tasks now required and a 5-minute margin, an average learner who does setup inside the block has less buffer than the headline implies. Evidence: README line 3: 'one 40-minute lab block ... sized to finish in about 35 minutes with a buffer left over inside the block'. README line 29: 'About 200 MB of free disk space for the test browser, and a network connection for the one-time setup.'. lab.json minutes.notes break the 35 minutes into tasks 1-6 (25) and 7-10 (10) only; no setup or reading allowance.
findings.recommendation: State in the headline that setup is done before the block (or fold a setup allowance into the estimate and cap).

items.note: Resolved on HEAD 9ad7bb04c287912d37605ba365b448f0fd68cd88. All ten tasks keep Where/Outcome/Done-when plus two partial hints; no completed CSS rule or completed markup appears in README, starter comments or test names. Same evidence as the coding-lab item: learners still select and compose every property and element themselves; hints are staged and partial, failure messages name the unmet outcome. The new TODO markers make files and locations to edit clearer without disclosing answers. Objective claims (14) remain aligned to the eleven public tests.

Reopened by the review-fix. The previously resolved state kept the README headline free of a median and fenced tasks 7-10 as stretch. b67a731f makes all ten tasks required and puts a specific figure back in the learner headline: 'sized to finish in about 35 minutes with a buffer left over inside the block'. The README does not label that figure an authoring re-estimate (only lab.json notes do), and it is half the prior authored estimate for this same ten-task scope (70 median / 90 cap) with no pilot or timing evidence added; the cap leaves a 5-minute margin and excludes README reading and the one-time Chromium setup. A task-by-task walk of the current tasks (viewport meta, two Flexbox rules, a desktop-first-to-mobile-first rewrite, a grid-area map inside a 1000px query, an overflow fix, then four markup repairs, each with test reruns of several seconds) puts an average newly-taught learner nearer 45 minutes than 35. To close: in the README headline label the minutes an authoring estimate, not a measured pilot, and either raise median/cap to an honest figure with a real buffer (S21's Guided lab leaves 62 minutes for this lab per intake section Minute budgets, so e.g. about 45 median / 55 cap stays inside both the block and the 30-60 module-lab range) or record measured pilot timing that supports 35/40.
